q: The differential equation of SHM, d^2x/dt^2 = -omega^2 x, shows that acceleration is
o: directly proportional to displacement and in the same direction
directly proportional to displacement and opposite in direction
why: The negative sign shows acceleration is proportional to x but directed opposite to displacement (restoring)

q: For a particle in SHM with x = A sin(omega t), the velocity is given by
why: Velocity in SHM: v = omega sqrt(A^2 - x^2)

q: The velocity of a particle in SHM is maximum at
o: midway between mean and extreme position
why: At mean position x = 0, v = omega A, which is the maximum value

q: The total energy of a particle executing SHM with amplitude A is
why: Total energy in SHM: E = (1/2) m omega^2 A^2, constant throughout the motion

q: The time period of a simple pendulum of length L is given by
why: Simple pendulum period: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g)

For a spring-mass system with spring constant k and mass m, the time period of oscillation is
why: Spring-mass system period: T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k)

q: The epoch of an SHM is defined as
o: the total phase angle omega t + phi
the value of phase at t = 0, i.e. phi
why: Epoch is the initial phase phi, the value of the phase angle at t = 0

q: In damped oscillations, the amplitude of the oscillating system
o: oscillates between zero and a maximum
why: Damping forces dissipate energy, causing the amplitude to decay exponentially with time

q: Resonance in forced oscillations occurs when
o: the driving frequency is much greater than natural frequency
the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the system
why: At resonance, driving frequency = natural frequency, giving maximum amplitude of oscillation
